correct_completion: I used to play in the park every day.
full_sentence: When I was a child, I used to play in the park every day.
acceptable_variants: I would play in the park every day.
I often played in the park.

options.text: I am playing in the park now.
options.why_wrong: The present continuous describes an action happening now, but the stem sets a past time, so a past habit is needed.

options.text: I used to play in the park every day.
I will play in the park tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense refers to tomorrow, but the stem is about the past, so it does not fit.

options.text: I have played in the park.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect does not describe a repeated past habit with 'every day', and it does not fit the time set by 'when I was a child'.

grammar_focus: Used to for past habits and repeated actions
explanation: The stem sets a past time, so the completion must describe a past habit. 'Used to' plus the base verb shows a repeated action that no longer happens. Learners often confuse it with the present perfect, which does not express a finished habit.
translation: Quando eu era criança, eu costumava brincar no parque todos os dias.
